1.topic: Ìkíni àti ọ̀rọ̀ ìwà ọmọlúwàbí (Greetings and courtesy)
1.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. greet correctly at different times of the day (morning, afternoon, evening, night) and on different occasions;
2. use the common expressions of courtesy (thanks, please, apology, sympathy) in the right place;
3. show the traditional way a Yoruba child greets an elder, and explain why the plural form "ẹ" is used for elders.

## Materials

Picture cards showing a morning scene, a market at noon, a family at dinner and a person returning from a journey; a mat for demonstrating kneeling and prostrating; chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Without saying anything, the teacher walks into the class and waits. Ask in Yoruba: "Kí ni ó yẹ kí ẹ sọ?" (What should you say?) Let pupils offer greetings. Write the correct ones on the board with full tone marks and under-dots.

## Development

1. Teach the greetings by time of day: Ẹ káàárọ̀, Ẹ kú ọ̀sán, Ẹ kú ìrọ̀lẹ́, Ó dàárọ̀. Pupils repeat in chorus, then in rows, then in pairs.
2. Teach the greetings by occasion: Ẹ kú iṣẹ́ (to someone working), Ẹ káàbọ̀ (welcome), Ẹ kú àbọ̀ (to someone returning), Ẹ kú ilé (to someone at home). Show the reply for each.
3. Teach the courtesy words: Ẹ ṣé (thank you), Ẹ jọ̀ọ́ (please), Ẹ má bínú (sorry, do not be angry), Ẹ pẹ̀lẹ́ (sympathy).
4. Explain that a Yoruba child uses "ẹ" for an elder even when speaking to one person. Demonstrate that boys traditionally prostrate (dọ̀bálẹ̀) and girls kneel (kúnlẹ̀). Many families now use a slight bow; accept the practice of the home.
5. Stress writing: copy each greeting with every tone mark and under-dot. A greeting written "E kaaro" is incomplete.

## Class activity

In pairs, one pupil plays a visitor and the other plays an elder at home. They greet, ask after the family, and say thanks. Swap roles.

## Evaluation

1. What do you say to a person who is working?
2. Write the greeting for the afternoon with its tone marks.
3. Why do we say "ẹ" to one elder?

## Assignment

Worksheet on the app, due Friday.

reading.content:
# Ìkíni ní ilẹ̀ Yorùbá

Ní ilẹ̀ Yorùbá, ìkíni ṣe pàtàkì púpọ̀. Bí a bá pàdé ẹnìkan, a máa kọ́kọ́ kí i kí a tó sọ nǹkan mìíràn. Ìkíni jẹ́ ara ìwà ọmọlúwàbí. Ọmọ tí kò bá mọ ìkíni kò ì tíì kọ́ ìwà.

## Ìkíni ní àkókò ọjọ́

- **Ẹ káàárọ̀**: a máa ń sọ ọ́ ní àárọ̀.
- **Ẹ kú ọ̀sán**: a máa ń sọ ọ́ ní ọ̀sán.
- **Ẹ kú ìrọ̀lẹ́**: a máa ń sọ ọ́ ní ìrọ̀lẹ́.
- **Ó dàárọ̀**: a máa ń sọ ọ́ kí a tó lọ sùn.

Ẹni tí a kí máa ń dáhùn pé "Ẹ káàárọ̀", tàbí "Ẹ ṣé".

## Ìkíni ní ìgbà ọ̀tọ̀ọ̀tọ̀

- **Ẹ kú iṣẹ́**: a máa ń sọ ọ́ fún ẹni tí ó ń ṣiṣẹ́.
- **Ẹ káàbọ̀**: a máa ń sọ ọ́ fún àlejò tí ó dé ilé wa.
- **Ẹ kú àbọ̀**: a máa ń sọ ọ́ fún ẹni tí ó dé láti ìrìn-àjò.
- **Ẹ kú ilé**: a máa ń sọ ọ́ fún ẹni tí a bá nílé.

## Ìbéèrè nípa ìlera

Ìbéèrè: Báwo ni?
Ìdáhùn: Mo wà dáadáa. Ẹ ṣé.

Ìbéèrè: Ṣé àlàáfíà ni?
Ìdáhùn: Àlàáfíà ni.

## Ọ̀rọ̀ ìwà ọmọlúwàbí

- **Ẹ ṣé** túmọ̀ sí "thank you".
- **Ẹ jọ̀ọ́** túmọ̀ sí "please".
- **Ẹ má bínú** túmọ̀ sí "sorry, do not be angry".
- **Ẹ pẹ̀lẹ́** ni a máa ń sọ fún ẹni tí ó wà nínú ìṣòro tàbí tí ó ń ṣiṣẹ́ àṣekára.

## Báwo ni ọmọ Yorùbá ṣe ń kí àgbà?

Ọmọkùnrin máa ń dọ̀bálẹ̀, ọmọbìnrin sì máa ń kúnlẹ̀ nígbà tí wọ́n bá ń kí àgbà. A tún máa ń lo "ẹ" fún àgbà, bí ó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ ẹnìkan ṣoṣo ni a ń bá sọ̀rọ̀. Èyí jẹ́ àmì ọ̀wọ̀.

## Ìjíròrò kúkúrú

Olùkọ́: Ẹ káàárọ̀, ẹ̀yin ọmọ.
Àwọn ọmọ: Ẹ káàárọ̀, Olùkọ́.
Olùkọ́: Báwo ni ẹ ṣe wà?
Àwọn ọmọ: A wà dáadáa. Ẹ ṣé.

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Bí a bá ń kọ ìkíni, a gbọdọ̀ kọ gbogbo àmì ohùn àti ẹ̀ṣẹ̀-ìsàlẹ̀: Ẹ káàárọ̀, kì í ṣe "E kaaro".

2.topic: Ohùn àti ìró Yorùbá (Tones and sounds)
2.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. name the three Yoruba tones (ohùn òkè, ohùn àárín, ohùn ìsàlẹ̀) and mark them;
2. pronounce and write minimal pairs that differ only in tone or in the under-dotted letters;
3. pronounce the nasal vowels and the consonant gb correctly.

## Materials

A drum or a ruler for tapping the rhythm of words, cards with the minimal pairs written large, a drawing of a hand sloping up and down to show tone, chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Write ọkọ on the board without any mark. Ask pupils what it means. Different pupils will give husband, vehicle, hoe. Tell them that all three are written ọkọ without marks and that the marks tell us which is meant.

## Development

1. Teach the three tones with the hand gesture: high (ohùn òkè, acute mark ´) with the hand rising, low (ohùn ìsàlẹ̀, grave mark `) with the hand falling, and mid (ohùn àárín) with the hand level. The mid tone has no mark.
2. Drill the set ọkọ (husband), ọkọ̀ (vehicle), ọkọ́ (hoe), ọ̀kọ̀ (spear). Then owó (money), ọwọ́ (hand), òwò (trade). Pupils tap each syllable while saying it.
3. Show that the letters ẹ, ọ and ṣ change words: ṣe (do, make) and sè (cook); owó and ọwọ́.
4. Teach the nasal vowels an, ẹn, in, ọn, un with words such as ọkùnrin, obìnrin, ẹ̀gbọ́n, ìrìn. Pupils feel the air in the nose.
5. Teach gb as one sound, with gbé (carry) and gé (cut).
6. Pupils write each word with all marks. Correct mistakes at once.

## Class activity

The teacher says a word without showing it; pupils write it with tone marks on slates and hold it up. Count correct answers by row.

## Evaluation

1. How many tones are there in Yoruba?
2. Write the word for "hoe".
3. What is the difference between owó and ọwọ́?

## Assignment

Quiz on the app, due Friday.

reading.title: Ohùn Yorùbá àti bí a ṣe ń pe ọ̀rọ̀
reading.content:
# Ohùn Yorùbá àti bí a ṣe ń pe ọ̀rọ̀

Èdè Yorùbá jẹ́ èdè oníhùn. Èyí túmọ̀ sí pé ohùn tí a fi pe ọ̀rọ̀ kan lè yí ìtumọ̀ rẹ̀ padà. Nítorí náà, a gbọdọ̀ kọ àmì ohùn dáadáa.

## Ohùn mẹ́ta

Ohùn mẹ́ta ni ó wà nínú èdè Yorùbá:

1. **Ohùn òkè**: a kọ ọ́ báyìí ´. Àpẹẹrẹ: **ọwọ́**, **owó**, **ilé**.
2. **Ohùn ìsàlẹ̀**: a kọ ọ́ báyìí `. Àpẹẹrẹ: **òwò**, **bàtà**, **ọ̀kọ̀**.
3. **Ohùn àárín**: a kò kọ àmì sí i. Àpẹẹrẹ: **ọmọ**, **ẹja**, **aṣọ**.

Bí a bá fẹ́ pe ohùn òkè, ohùn wa gbọdọ̀ gòkè. Bí a bá fẹ́ pe ohùn ìsàlẹ̀, ohùn wa gbọdọ̀ sọ̀kalẹ̀. Fún ohùn àárín, ohùn wa dúró ní àárín.

## Ọ̀rọ̀ tí ohùn ṣe ìyàtọ̀ wọn

| Ọ̀rọ̀ | Ìtumọ̀ |
| --- | --- |
| ọkọ | husband |
| ọkọ̀ | vehicle, boat |
| ọkọ́ | hoe |
| ọ̀kọ̀ | spear |
| owó | money |
| ọwọ́ | hand |
| òwò | trade |

Ẹ ṣàkíyèsí pé nínú **owó** àti **ọwọ́**, ìyàtọ̀ tún wà nínú ẹ̀ṣẹ̀-ìsàlẹ̀: **o** àti **ọ** kì í ṣe lẹ́tà kan náà.

Ìyàtọ̀ tún wà láàrin **ṣe** (to do, to make) àti **sè** (to cook). Ìyá mi ń sè oúnjẹ. Bàbá mi ń ṣiṣẹ́.

## Fáwẹ́ẹ̀lì àránmúpè

Èdè Yorùbá ní fáwẹ́ẹ̀lì àránmúpè márùn-ún: **an, ẹn, in, ọn, un**. A pè wọ́n pẹ̀lú ímú. Àpẹẹrẹ: **ọkùnrin**, **obìnrin**, **ẹ̀gbọ́n**, **ìrìn**.

## Ìró "gb"

"gb" jẹ́ ìró kan ṣoṣo, bí ó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ pé a fi lẹ́tà méjì kọ ọ́. A kò pe g àti b lọ́tọ̀ọ̀tọ̀. Àpẹẹrẹ: **gbé** (to carry), **gbà** (to take, to receive). Ó yàtọ̀ sí **gé** (to cut).

## Bí a ṣe lè ṣe ìdánrawò

1. Gbọ́ ọ̀rọ̀ náà láti ẹnu olùkọ́.
2. Pe ọ̀rọ̀ náà lẹ́ẹ̀mẹta.
3. Tẹ ìró ọ̀rọ̀ náà lórí tábìlì, ìró kan fún sílébù kan.
4. Kọ ọ̀rọ̀ náà pẹ̀lú gbogbo àmì rẹ̀.

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

- Ohùn mẹ́ta ni ó wà: òkè, àárín àti ìsàlẹ̀.
- Àmì ohùn àti ẹ̀ṣẹ̀-ìsàlẹ̀ lè yí ìtumọ̀ ọ̀rọ̀ padà.
- "gb" jẹ́ ìró kan.

3.topic: Ìjíròrò àti eré ìṣeré (Dialogues and role plays)
3.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. introduce themselves and ask others for their names, ages and homes;
2. carry out a short dialogue at the market and at school using correct greetings and polite words;
3. take turns correctly in a role play and mark who is speaking.

## Materials

Toy money or paper naira notes, pictures of tomatoes, pepper and onions, a small table to act as a market stall, a chalkboard for the speaker labels.

## Starter (5 minutes)

The teacher plays the seller and a pupil the buyer. The teacher says "Ẹ káàbọ̀" and waits. Ask the class what the buyer should say next. Collect the lines on the board.

## Development

1. Teach the introduction frame: Orúkọ mi ni ___. Ọmọ ọdún mẹ́wàá ni mí. Mo ń gbé ní ___. Mo wà ní kíláàsì kínní. Pupils practise in pairs.
2. Teach the market dialogue: Ẹ kú ọjà. Èló ni? Ọgọ́rùn-ún náírà ni. Ó wọ́n jù. Ẹ dín in kù. Ẹ ṣé. Practise each line with the right tone.
3. Teach the classroom dialogue: Ẹ jókòó. Ẹ dìde. Ẹ ṣí ìwé yín. Ẹ jọ̀ọ́, mo fẹ́ lọ sí ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀.
4. Show how to write a dialogue: the speaker's name, a colon, then the words. Each new speaker begins on a new line.
5. Remind pupils to use "ẹ" for elders and "o" for friends of their own age.
6. Pupils present in front of the class. The class says one thing that was done well and one thing to improve.

## Class activity

Groups of three act "Ní ọjà": a seller, a buyer and a friend who arrives to tell the buyer it is time to go home. Each group writes its dialogue in the speaker-colon format.

## Evaluation

1. How do you ask for the price of an item?
2. What does a pupil say to ask permission to leave the class?
3. Write two lines of a dialogue between a teacher and a pupil.

## Assignment

Problem set on the app, due Friday.

reading.title: Ìjíròrò ojoojúmọ́
reading.content:
# Ìjíròrò ojoojúmọ́

Ìjíròrò ni ọ̀rọ̀ tí àwọn ènìyàn méjì tàbí jù bẹ́ẹ̀ lọ ń sọ láàrin ara wọn. Ní ojoojúmọ́, a máa ń bá àwọn ènìyàn sọ̀rọ̀ ní ilé, ní ilé ìwé àti ní ọjà. Ó dára kí a mọ bí a ṣe lè sọ̀rọ̀ ní ọ̀nà tí ó bá ìwà ọmọlúwàbí mu.

## Ìfinipè ara ẹni (Introducing yourself)

Tọ́pẹ́: Ẹ káàárọ̀. Orúkọ mi ni Tọ́pẹ́.
Ayọ̀: Ẹ káàárọ̀. Orúkọ tèmi ni Ayọ̀.
Tọ́pẹ́: Ọmọ ọdún mẹ́wàá ni mí. Mo ń gbé ní Ìbàdàn.
Ayọ̀: Èmi náà ń gbé ní Ìbàdàn. Mo wà ní kíláàsì kínní.

## Ní ọjà (At the market)

Oníbàárà: Ẹ kú ọjà, ìyá.
Olùtajà: Ẹ ṣé. Ẹ káàbọ̀. Kí ni ẹ fẹ́?
Oníbàárà: Mo fẹ́ ra tòmátì. Èló ni?
Olùtajà: Ọgọ́rùn-ún náírà ni.
Oníbàárà: Ó wọ́n jù. Ẹ dín in kù.
Olùtajà: Ó dára. Mo dín in kù. Ẹ gbà á.
Oníbàárà: Ẹ ṣé, ìyá.

## Ní ilé ìwé (At school)

Olùkọ́: Ẹ káàárọ̀, ẹ̀yin ọmọ.
Àwọn ọmọ: Ẹ káàárọ̀, Olùkọ́.
Olùkọ́: Ẹ jókòó. Ẹ ṣí ìwé yín.
Ọmọ kan: Ẹ jọ̀ọ́, Olùkọ́, mo fẹ́ lọ sí ilé ìgbọ̀nsẹ̀.
Olùkọ́: Ó dára. Lọ, kí o sì padà wá yára.

## Bí a ṣe ń kọ ìjíròrò

1. Kọ orúkọ ẹni tí ó ń sọ̀rọ̀ síwájú.
2. Fi àmì ìdánudúró (:) sí ẹ̀yìn orúkọ rẹ̀.
3. Kọ ohun tí ó sọ.
4. Bí ẹlòmíràn bá ń sọ̀rọ̀, bẹ̀rẹ̀ ní ìlà tuntun.

## Ọ̀rọ̀ tí ó wúlò

- **Èló ni?** (How much is it?)
- **Ó wọ́n jù.** (It is too expensive.)
- **Ẹ dín in kù.** (Reduce it.)
- **Ẹ jókòó.** (Sit down.) **Ẹ dìde.** (Stand up.)

## Ìkìlọ̀

Fún àgbà, a máa ń lo "ẹ" àti "yín". Fún ọ̀rẹ́ tí ó jọ wa lọ́jọ́ orí, a lè lo "o" àti "rẹ".

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Ìjíròrò rere ní ìkíni, ọ̀rọ̀ tí ó ṣe kedere, àti ìdúpẹ́ ní ìparí.

4.topic: Òwe, ewì, ìjálá àti rárà (Proverbs and oral poetry)
4.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. recite at least three Yoruba proverbs and explain what each means;
2. say what ewì, ìjálá and rárà are, and who performs or uses each;
3. use a proverb correctly in a short spoken or written sentence.

## Materials

Proverbs written on strips of card, a picture of a hunter with his gun and dog, a short recording or live demonstration of a chant (if a parent or community elder can come), chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Ask a pupil to repeat something an elder at home often says as advice. Collect two or three. Tell the class that many such sayings are òwe (proverbs) and that Yoruba people say, "Òwe lẹ́ṣin ọ̀rọ̀" (a proverb is the horse of speech).

## Development

1. Read each proverb aloud twice and have the class repeat: Iṣẹ́ ni oògùn ìṣẹ́. Àgbà kì í wà lọ́jà kí orí ọmọ titun wọ́. Ọmọ tí a kò kọ́ ni yóò gbé ilé tà. Òwe lẹ́ṣin ọ̀rọ̀; bí ọ̀rọ̀ bá sọnù, òwe ni a fi ń wá a.
2. For each proverb ask: what does it say on the surface and what does it mean? Write the meaning in simple Yoruba and in English on the board.
3. Define ewì as poetry that is carefully shaped and pleasing to the ear. Ìjálá is the chanted poetry of hunters in honour of Ògún, the patron of hunters. Rárà is another form of chanted poetry used to praise people, families and towns. (Check the local practice of your community and tell pupils where the chanting is heard.)
4. Play or demonstrate a chant. Ask pupils what is different from ordinary speech: rhythm, repetition, praise, rising voice.
5. Practise the use of a proverb in a sentence: Bàbá mi sọ pé iṣẹ́ ni oògùn ìṣẹ́, nítorí náà mo ń ṣiṣẹ́ àṣekára.
6. Remind pupils to write each proverb with all tone marks and under-dots, since a missing mark can change the meaning.

## Class activity

In groups, each pupil takes one proverb and acts a short scene in which it fits. The class guesses the proverb.

## Evaluation

1. Who performs ìjálá?
2. What does "Iṣẹ́ ni oògùn ìṣẹ́" mean?
3. Why do Yoruba speakers use proverbs?

## Assignment

Worksheet on the app, due Friday.

# Òwe àti ewì Yorùbá

Àwọn Yorùbá kì í sọ ọ̀rọ̀ lásán. Wọ́n fẹ́ràn òwe, ewì àti orin. Àwọn nǹkan wọ̀nyí jẹ́ ara àṣà àti ọgbọ́n ìbílẹ̀ wa.

## Òwe

Òwe ni ọ̀rọ̀ kúkúrú tí ó ní ọgbọ́n nínú. Àwọn Yorùbá sọ pé, "**Òwe lẹ́ṣin ọ̀rọ̀; bí ọ̀rọ̀ bá sọnù, òwe ni a fi ń wá a.**" Èyí túmọ̀ sí pé òwe ń ràn wá lọ́wọ́ láti sọ ohun tí a fẹ́ sọ ní kíkún.

### Àpẹẹrẹ òwe

1. **Iṣẹ́ ni oògùn ìṣẹ́.**
   Ìtumọ̀: Ṣíṣe iṣẹ́ ni ọ̀nà láti bọ́ lọ́wọ́ òṣì. (Work is the cure for poverty.)

2. **Àgbà kì í wà lọ́jà kí orí ọmọ titun wọ́.**
   Ìtumọ̀: Bí àgbà bá wà ní àárín wa, ó ń tọ́ ọmọdé sọ́nà. (Where an elder is present, a child is guided.)

3. **Ọmọ tí a kò kọ́ ni yóò gbé ilé tà.**
   Ìtumọ̀: Ọmọ tí a kò kọ́ ní ẹ̀kọ́ ilé lè ba ohun ìní ẹbí jẹ́. (A child who is not taught may waste the family's property.)

Bí a bá ń lo òwe, a gbọdọ̀ lò ó níbi tí ó yẹ. Àpẹẹrẹ: Bàbá mi sọ pé iṣẹ́ ni oògùn ìṣẹ́, nítorí náà mo ń ṣiṣẹ́ àṣekára.

## Ewì

Ewì ni ọ̀rọ̀ tí a ṣe lọ́ṣọ̀ọ́, tí ó sì dùn létí. A lè kọ ọ́, a sì lè sọ ọ́ lẹ́nu. Ewì ní ìró, ìdàpọ̀ ọ̀rọ̀ àti ìtumọ̀ jíjinlẹ̀. Oríṣìíríṣìí ewì ló wà, bíi ìjálá àti rárà.

## Ìjálá

Ìjálá jẹ́ ewì alohùn tí àwọn ọdẹ ń kọ. Wọ́n ń yin Ògún, ọlọ́run ọdẹ, wọ́n sì ń sọ nípa iṣẹ́ ọdẹ, ìgboyà àti àwọn baba ńlá wọn. A máa ń gbọ́ ìjálá ní ibi ayẹyẹ ọdẹ àti ní ibi ìsìnkú ọdẹ.

## Rárà

Rárà jẹ́ ewì alohùn tí a ń kọ láti yin ènìyàn, ẹbí àti ìlú. Ẹni tí ó ń kọ ọ́ máa ń ké ní ohùn gíga.

## Àǹfààní òwe àti ewì

- Wọ́n ń kọ́ ọmọdé ní ìwà rere.
- Wọ́n ń mú kí a rántí ìtàn àti orúkọ àwọn baba wa.
- Wọ́n ń mú kí ọ̀rọ̀ dùn, kí ó sì rí ìtumọ̀ jíjinlẹ̀.

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Bí a bá ń kọ òwe, a gbọdọ̀ kọ gbogbo àmì ohùn àti ẹ̀ṣẹ̀-ìsàlẹ̀ rẹ̀. Ìyàtọ̀ wà láàrin **iṣẹ́** (work) àti **ìṣẹ́** (poverty).

5.topic: Ìtàn àlọ́ àti àlọ́ àpamọ̀ (Folktales and riddles)
5.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. listen to a Yoruba folktale and retell it in their own words in the right order;
2. state the lesson of a folktale;
3. solve and explain simple riddles and say how a riddle differs from a folktale.

## Materials

A picture of a tortoise (ìjàpá) and a yam farm, a needle or a picture of one, a mat for the class to sit on in a circle, chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Seat the class in a circle. The teacher opens with "Àlọ́ o!" and the class answers "Àlọ́!". Explain that this is how Yoruba folktales and riddles begin and that the answer from the class means "we are ready to listen".

## Development

1. Tell the story "Ìjàpá àti iṣu" slowly, twice. The second time ask questions in Yoruba after every two sentences: Ta ni ó wà nínú ìtàn? Kí ló ṣẹlẹ̀?
2. Write four key words on the board: ebi (hunger), oko (farm), olè (thief), ẹ̀kọ́ (lesson).
3. Pupils retell the story in order in pairs: ibi tí ó ti ṣẹlẹ̀, ohun tí ó ṣẹlẹ̀, ìparí. Move round and listen.
4. Teach that ìtàn àlọ́ (folktale) is a story with a lesson, often told at night, and àlọ́ àpamọ̀ (riddle) is a short question whose answer is hidden and which tests the wit of the listener.
5. Present two riddles and let pupils answer: Ó ní ojú ṣùgbọ́n kò lè ríran. (Abẹ́rẹ́.) Ó ń fi ikùn rìn. (Ejò.) Ask pupils why the answer fits.
6. Pupils copy the story's lesson and the riddles with all tone marks.

## Class activity

Each pupil asks the class a riddle they have heard at home. The rest answer. Pupils who cannot answer may ask for a clue.

## Evaluation

1. Who is the main character of the story?
2. What lesson does the story teach?
3. What is the answer to "Ó ní ojú ṣùgbọ́n kò lè ríran"?

## Assignment

Worksheet on the app, due Friday.

reading.title: Ìjàpá àti iṣu
reading.content:
# Ìjàpá àti iṣu

Àlọ́ o! — Àlọ́.

Ní ọjọ́ kan, ebi ń pa Ìjàpá gan-an. Ó lọ sí oko kan tí wọ́n ti gbin iṣu púpọ̀. Nígbà tí ó dé ibẹ̀, kò rí ẹnìkankan. Ó wa iṣu méjì, ó sì fi wọ́n sínú àpò rẹ̀.

Àgbẹ̀ tí ó ni oko náà dé lójijì. Nígbà tí ó rí Ìjàpá, ó kígbe pé, "Ẹ mú olè! Ẹ mú olè!" Ìjàpá bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí sá lọ. Ó sá, ó sá, ó sá. Nínú ìbẹ̀rù rẹ̀, ó sọ àpò iṣu náà nù.

Ó padà sílé pẹ̀lú ebi, ó sì ń sunkún. Láti ọjọ́ náà, Ìjàpá kò jalè mọ́.

Ìtàn mi dópin níbí.

## Ẹ̀kọ́ tí ìtàn yìí kọ́ wa

Olè jíjà kò dára. Bí a bá jalè, a lè sá, ṣùgbọ́n a kò ní jẹ ohun tí a jí. Ó dára kí a ṣiṣẹ́ fún oúnjẹ wa.

## Ìtàn àlọ́ àti àlọ́ àpamọ̀

**Ìtàn àlọ́** jẹ́ ìtàn tí a ń sọ, tí ó sì ní ẹ̀kọ́ nínú. Àwọn ìtàn àlọ́ pọ̀ nípa ẹranko, bíi Ìjàpá, tí ó jẹ́ alárékérekè. A máa ń sọ wọ́n ní alẹ́ nígbà tí gbogbo ẹbí bá péjọ.

**Àlọ́ àpamọ̀** jẹ́ ìbéèrè kúkúrú tí ìdáhùn rẹ̀ pamọ́. A fi ń dán ọgbọ́n ẹni wò.

Bí a bá fẹ́ bẹ̀rẹ̀ àlọ́, a máa ń sọ pé "Àlọ́ o!", àwọn olùgbọ́ yóò sì dáhùn pé "Àlọ́!".

### Àpẹẹrẹ àlọ́ àpamọ̀

Àlọ́ o! — Àlọ́.
Ó ní ojú ṣùgbọ́n kò lè ríran.
Ìdáhùn: **Abẹ́rẹ́**. Abẹ́rẹ́ ní ihò tí a ń pè ní ojú, ṣùgbọ́n kò lè ríran.

Àlọ́ o! — Àlọ́.
Ó ń fi ikùn rìn.
Ìdáhùn: **Ejò**.

## Bí a ṣe ń tún ìtàn sọ

1. Sọ ibi tí ìtàn ti ṣẹlẹ̀.
2. Sọ ohun tí ó ṣẹlẹ̀ ní ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan, ní ìlànà.
3. Sọ bí ìtàn náà ṣe parí.
4. Sọ ẹ̀kọ́ tí ó kọ́ wa.

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Ìtàn àlọ́ ní ẹ̀kọ́. Àlọ́ àpamọ̀ ní ìdáhùn tí a gbọdọ̀ wá.

6.topic: Álífábẹ́ẹ̀tì Yorùbá: lẹ́tà, fáwẹ́ẹ̀lì, kọ́ńsónáǹtì àti àmì ohùn
6.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. recite and write the 25 letters of the Yoruba alphabet;
2. name the oral vowels, the nasal vowels and the consonants;
3. write words and short sentences with the under-dotted letters (ẹ, ọ, ṣ) and the tone marks.

## Materials

A large chart of the Yoruba alphabet, letter cards, slates or notebooks, a list of words with under-dots, chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Ask pupils to say the English vowels. Then ask: are they the same as the Yoruba vowels? Write a, e, i, o, u on the left and a, e, ẹ, i, o, ọ, u on the right, and ask which are missing from the left.

## Development

1. Teach the 25 letters in order: a, b, d, e, ẹ, f, g, gb, h, i, j, k, l, m, n, o, ọ, p, r, s, ṣ, t, u, w, y. Pupils chant them in a rhythm and point at the chart.
2. Teach the groups: seven oral vowels (a, e, ẹ, i, o, ọ, u), five nasal vowels (an, ẹn, in, ọn, un) and eighteen consonants (b, d, f, g, gb, h, j, k, l, m, n, p, r, s, ṣ, t, w, y).
3. Point out that c, q, v, x and z are not in the Yoruba alphabet and that gb is one letter written with two characters.
4. Teach the under-dot: ẹ, ọ and ṣ are separate letters. Contrast e and ẹ (ẹja, èrò), o and ọ (owó, ọwọ́), s and ṣ (sùn, ṣe).
5. Teach the tone marks: ´ for high, ` for low, no mark for mid. Write sample words and ask pupils to add the marks.
6. Pupils copy the alphabet in their notebooks and underline the letters with under-dots.

## Class activity

Dictation of ten words and two short sentences. Pupils swap papers and mark each other's under-dots and tone marks.

## Evaluation

1. How many letters are in the Yoruba alphabet?
2. Write the seven oral vowels.
3. Which letters have under-dots?

## Assignment

Worksheet on the app, due Friday.

reading.content:
# Álífábẹ́ẹ̀tì Yorùbá

Álífábẹ́ẹ̀tì Yorùbá ní lẹ́tà márùn-dínlọ́gbọ̀n (25). Àwọn lẹ́tà náà nìyí:

**a, b, d, e, ẹ, f, g, gb, h, i, j, k, l, m, n, o, ọ, p, r, s, ṣ, t, u, w, y**

Àwọn lẹ́tà bíi c, q, v, x àti z kò sí nínú álífábẹ́ẹ̀tì Yorùbá.

## Fáwẹ́ẹ̀lì

Fáwẹ́ẹ̀lì ni ìró tí a pè láìsí ìdíwọ́ fún afẹ́fẹ́ nínú ẹnu. Àwọn oríṣi méjì ni ó wà.

**1. Fáwẹ́ẹ̀lì àìránmúpè (oral vowels): méje**

a, e, ẹ, i, o, ọ, u

**2. Fáwẹ́ẹ̀lì àránmúpè (nasal vowels): márùn-ún**

an, ẹn, in, ọn, un

Àpẹẹrẹ: ọkùnrin (man), obìnrin (woman), ìrìn (walking).

Ẹ ṣàkíyèsí pé fáwẹ́ẹ̀lì Gẹ̀ẹ́sì márùn-ún (a, e, i, o, u) kò tó fún èdè Yorùbá. A nílò **ẹ** àti **ọ** pẹ̀lú.

## Kọ́ńsónáǹtì

Kọ́ńsónáǹtì jẹ́ ìró tí a pè pẹ̀lú ìdíwọ́ fún afẹ́fẹ́. Méjìdínlógún (18) ni wọ́n:

b, d, f, g, gb, h, j, k, l, m, n, p, r, s, ṣ, t, w, y

Ẹ ṣàkíyèsí pé **gb** jẹ́ lẹ́tà kan, bí ó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ pé a fi àmì méjì kọ ọ́.

## Lẹ́tà tí ó ní ẹ̀ṣẹ̀-ìsàlẹ̀

Ẹ̀ṣẹ̀-ìsàlẹ̀ ni àmì kékeré tí a fi sí abẹ́ lẹ́tà. Lẹ́tà mẹ́ta ló ní i: **ẹ, ọ, ṣ**.

| Láìsí ẹ̀ṣẹ̀-ìsàlẹ̀ | Pẹ̀lú ẹ̀ṣẹ̀-ìsàlẹ̀ |
| --- | --- |
| owó (money) | ọwọ́ (hand) |
| sè (to cook) | ṣe (to do) |

Ìyàtọ̀ tí ó rọrùn: **ẹja** (fish) àti **iṣu** (yam). Bí a bá kọ wọ́n láìsí ẹ̀ṣẹ̀-ìsàlẹ̀ (eja, isu), àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ náà kò tọ́.

## Àmì ohùn

- Ohùn òkè: ´ (á)
- Ohùn ìsàlẹ̀: ` (à)
- Ohùn àárín: kò ní àmì (a)

Àpẹẹrẹ gbólóhùn tí a kọ ní ọ̀nà tí ó tọ́: **Ìbàdàn ni ilé mi.**

## Bí a ṣe ń kọ ọ́

1. Kọ lẹ́tà kọ̀ọ̀kan ní kedere.
2. Fi ẹ̀ṣẹ̀-ìsàlẹ̀ sí abẹ́ ẹ, ọ àti ṣ.
3. Fi àmì ohùn sí orí fáwẹ́ẹ̀lì tàbí sí orí n tí ó jẹ́ sílébù.
4. Tún ohun tí o kọ ṣe àyẹ̀wò.

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Lẹ́tà Yorùbá jẹ́ márùn-dínlọ́gbọ̀n. Fáwẹ́ẹ̀lì àìránmúpè méje, àránmúpè márùn-ún àti kọ́ńsónáǹtì méjìdínlógún ni a ní.

1. write a simple Yoruba sentence in the right order (subject, verb, object);
2. join two simple sentences with sì, ṣùgbọ́n or tàbí to make a compound sentence;
3. make a complex sentence with nítorí pé, tí or bí ... bá, and say which kind of sentence they have written.

## Materials

Word cards that can be arranged into sentences, a long strip of paper for joining sentences, pictures of children at play, chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Give five pupils word cards: Ọmọ, náà, ń, kàwé, ní ilé. Ask them to stand in an order that makes a sentence. Let the class say whether it is correct. Write the right order on the board.

## Development

1. Teach the simple sentence with one subject and one verb: Ọmọ náà ń kàwé. Mo lọ sí ilé ìwé. Bàbá mi ń ṣiṣẹ́. Show that the order is subject, verb, object, as in English: Ọmọ náà jẹ ẹ̀bà.
2. Teach negation with kò or ò: Ọmọ náà kò jẹun. Mi ò jẹun. Warn against mixing the two: "Mo kò jẹun" is wrong.
3. Teach the compound sentence, made of two simple sentences joined by sì (and), ṣùgbọ́n (but) or tàbí (or): Mo lọ sí ọjà, mo sì ra iṣu. Bàbá mi ń ṣiṣẹ́ ṣùgbọ́n ìyá mi wà nílé.
4. Teach the complex sentence, with a main clause and a clause that depends on it: Mo dé ilé nítorí pé òjò ń rọ̀. Nígbà tí mo dé ilé, mo jẹun. Bí òjò bá rọ̀, a kò ní ṣeré lóde.
5. Practise: the teacher says a simple sentence, a pupil adds a joining word and a second part.
6. Remind pupils that the English labels (simple, compound, complex) are used in this lesson for convenience and the Yoruba examples carry the learning.

## Class activity

Sentence building relay. Each team receives a pile of cards and builds one simple, one compound and one complex sentence. The first team to build all three correctly, with tone marks, wins.

## Evaluation

1. Write a simple sentence about your school.
2. Join two simple sentences with ṣùgbọ́n.
3. Complete: Mo dúró nílé nítorí pé ____.

## Assignment

Quiz on the app, due Friday.

reading.content:
# Bí a ṣe ń kọ gbólóhùn Yorùbá

Gbólóhùn ni ọ̀rọ̀ tàbí àwùjọ ọ̀rọ̀ tí ó ní ìtumọ̀ kíkún. Ó gbọdọ̀ ní olùṣe iṣẹ́ (subject) àti ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe (verb). Àwọn oríṣi gbólóhùn mẹ́ta ni a máa kọ́kọ́ kọ́: kúkúrú (simple), àsopọ̀ (compound) àti oníṣọ̀kan (complex).

## 1. Gbólóhùn kúkúrú (simple sentence)

Gbólóhùn kúkúrú ní olùṣe iṣẹ́ kan àti ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe kan.

- Ọmọ náà ń kàwé.
- Mo lọ sí ilé ìwé.
- Bàbá mi ń ṣiṣẹ́.
- Ìyá mi ń sè oúnjẹ.

Ìlànà ọ̀rọ̀ nínú gbólóhùn ni: **olùṣe iṣẹ́ + ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe + àbọ̀** (subject, verb, object):

Ọmọ náà **jẹ** ẹ̀bà.

Ẹ ṣọ́ra: **Ẹ̀bà jẹ ọmọ náà** túmọ̀ sí pé ẹ̀bà ló jẹ ọmọ náà. Ìlànà ọ̀rọ̀ ṣe pàtàkì!

## Gbólóhùn àyọkúrò (negative)

- Ọmọ náà **kò** jẹun.
- **Mi ò** jẹun. (kì í ṣe "Mo kò jẹun")

## 2. Gbólóhùn àsopọ̀ (compound sentence)

A so gbólóhùn kúkúrú méjì pọ̀ pẹ̀lú **sì** (and), **ṣùgbọ́n** (but) tàbí **tàbí** (or).

- Mo lọ sí ọjà, mo **sì** ra iṣu.
- Bàbá mi ń ṣiṣẹ́ **ṣùgbọ́n** ìyá mi wà nílé.
- Ṣé o fẹ́ ìrẹsì **tàbí** ẹ̀bà?

## 3. Gbólóhùn oníṣọ̀kan (complex sentence)

Gbólóhùn oníṣọ̀kan ní gbólóhùn pàtàkì àti gbólóhùn tí ó gbẹ́kẹ̀lé e. Àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ ìsopọ̀ tí a máa ń lò ni **nítorí pé** (because), **nígbà tí** (when) àti **bí ... bá** (if).

- Mo dé ilé **nítorí pé** òjò ń rọ̀.
- **Nígbà tí** mo dé ilé, mo jẹun.
- **Bí** òjò **bá** rọ̀, a kò ní ṣeré lóde.

## Àwọn àṣìṣe tí ó wọ́pọ̀

1. Kíkọ ìlànà ọ̀rọ̀ Gẹ̀ẹ́sì: "Jẹ ẹ̀bà ọmọ náà" dípò "Ọmọ náà jẹ ẹ̀bà".
2. Lílo "Mo kò" dípò "Mi ò".
3. Gbígbàgbé olùṣe iṣẹ́: "Ń kàwé" dípò "Ó ń kàwé".

## Bí a ṣe lè mọ irú gbólóhùn

- Bí gbólóhùn kan bá ní ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe kan, ó jẹ́ kúkúrú.
- Bí a bá so méjì pọ̀ pẹ̀lú sì, ṣùgbọ́n tàbí tàbí, ó jẹ́ àsopọ̀.
- Bí ọ̀kan bá gbẹ́kẹ̀lé òmíràn pẹ̀lú nítorí pé, nígbà tí tàbí bí ... bá, ó jẹ́ oníṣọ̀kan.

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Gbólóhùn rere ní olùṣe iṣẹ́, ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe àti ìtumọ̀ kíkún. Kọ gbogbo àmì ohùn rẹ̀.

9.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. identify a noun (orúkọ), a pronoun (arọ́pò-orúkọ), a verb (ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe) and an adjective (ọ̀rọ̀ àpèjúwe) in a Yoruba sentence;
2. use the correct subject pronoun for the person (mo, o, ó, a, ẹ, wọ́n);
3. place an adjective after the noun it describes.

## Materials

Four large cards labelled orúkọ, arọ́pò-orúkọ, ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe and ọ̀rọ̀ àpèjúwe, word cards for ten nouns, six pronouns, eight verbs and eight adjectives, pins or tape.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Ask five pupils to come out and hold word cards that form the sentence "Ọmọ gíga náà jẹ ẹ̀bà." Ask the class: which word names a person? Which word tells what he did? Which word tells us how the child is?

## Development

1. Orúkọ names a person, place or thing: ọmọ, ilé, Ìbàdàn, ìwé, aṣọ, ẹ̀bà.
2. Arọ́pò-orúkọ stands in place of a noun. The subject pronouns are mo (I), o (you, singular), ó (he, she, it), a (we), ẹ (you, plural or respect) and wọ́n (they). The stronger forms are èmi, ìwọ, òun, àwa, ẹ̀yin and àwọn.
3. Ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe says what is done or what state something is in: jẹ, lọ, sùn, sáré, kọ, ṣeré.
4. Ọ̀rọ̀ àpèjúwe (adjective) tells more about a noun: ńlá (big), kékeré (small), pupa (red), funfun (white), dúdú (black), gíga (tall), rere (good). The adjective comes after the noun: aṣọ pupa, ilé ńlá, ọmọ rere. In English it comes before.
5. Warn against repeating the pronoun: "Ayọ̀ ó ń kàwé" is wrong. Say "Ayọ̀ ń kàwé" or "Ó ń kàwé".
6. Pupils sort the word cards under the four labels, then write sentences using one word from each group.

## Class activity

Make a "Sentence factory": each group builds five sentences from the card piles and underlines each part in a different colour. A second group checks the sentences.

## Evaluation

1. Give two nouns, two verbs and two adjectives.
2. What pronoun will you use for "my sister and I"?
3. Write "red cloth" in Yoruba.

## Assignment

Problem set on the app, due Friday.

reading.content:
# Orúkọ, arọ́pò-orúkọ, ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe àti ọ̀rọ̀ àpèjúwe

Gbogbo ọ̀rọ̀ tí a bá lò nínú gbólóhùn ni a lè pín sí ẹ̀ka. Ẹ jẹ́ kí a mọ mẹ́rin nínú wọn.

## 1. Orúkọ (noun)

Orúkọ ni ọ̀rọ̀ tí a fi ń pe ènìyàn, ẹranko, ibi tàbí nǹkan.

- Ènìyàn: ọmọ, bàbá, ìyá, olùkọ́
- Ibi: ilé, ọjà, Ìbàdàn, ilé ìwé
- Nǹkan: ìwé, aṣọ, ẹ̀bà, iṣu

## 2. Arọ́pò-orúkọ (pronoun)

Arọ́pò-orúkọ ni ọ̀rọ̀ tí a fi rọ́pò orúkọ.

| Ènìyàn | Arọ́pò-orúkọ olùṣe | Àpẹẹrẹ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Èmi (I) | mo | Mo lọ sí ilé ìwé. |
| Ìwọ (you) | o | O jẹun. |
| Òun (he, she) | ó | Ó ń kàwé. |
| Àwa (we) | a | A ń ṣeré. |
| Ẹ̀yin (you, plural) | ẹ | Ẹ jókòó. |
| Àwọn (they) | wọ́n | Wọ́n ń kọrin. |

Bí orúkọ bá ti jẹ́ olùṣe iṣẹ́, a kì í tún pe arọ́pò-orúkọ rẹ̀ lẹ́yìn rẹ̀. A kò sọ pé "Ayọ̀ ó ń kàwé." A sọ pé "**Ayọ̀ ń kàwé**" tàbí "**Ó ń kàwé**".

## 3. Ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe (verb)

Ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe sọ ohun tí a ṣe.

- jẹ (to eat), lọ (to go), sùn (to sleep), sáré (to run), ṣeré (to play), kọ (to write)

Àpẹẹrẹ: Ọmọ náà **jẹ** ẹ̀bà. Àwọn ọmọ **ń ṣeré**.

## 4. Ọ̀rọ̀ àpèjúwe (adjective)

Ọ̀rọ̀ àpèjúwe ń sọ bí orúkọ ṣe rí.

- ńlá (big), kékeré (small), pupa (red), funfun (white), dúdú (black), gíga (tall), rere (good)

Nínú Yorùbá, ọ̀rọ̀ àpèjúwe máa ń tẹ̀lé orúkọ:

- aṣọ **pupa** (red cloth)
- ilé **ńlá** (big house)
- ọmọ **rere** (good child)

Kì í ṣe "pupa aṣọ", bíi ti Gẹ̀ẹ́sì.

## Àpẹẹrẹ gbólóhùn tí ó ní gbogbo wọn

**Ọmọ gíga náà jẹ ẹ̀bà.**

- Ọmọ, ẹ̀bà: orúkọ
- gíga: ọ̀rọ̀ àpèjúwe
- jẹ: ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe

**Ó jẹ ẹ̀bà.** Níbí, "ó" jẹ́ arọ́pò-orúkọ.

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Orúkọ ń pe nǹkan. Arọ́pò-orúkọ ń rọ́pò orúkọ. Ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe ń sọ ohun tí a ṣe. Ọ̀rọ̀ àpèjúwe ń tẹ̀lé orúkọ.

10.topic: Àkókò, nọ́ńbà, ọjọ́ ọ̀sẹ̀ àti oṣù (Time, numbers, days and months)
10.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. count from one to ten in Yoruba and use the numbers with nouns (ọmọ márùn-ún, ìwé mẹ́wàá);
2. say the days of the week and the months of the year in Yoruba;
3. ask and tell the time on the hour using "aago".

## Materials

A clock with movable hands, a weekly timetable chart, seven cards for the days, twelve cards for the months, ten counters, chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Ask: what day is it today? Take the answer in English and then give the Yoruba name. Ask pupils to say the days they come to school and the days they stay at home.

## Development

1. Teach the counting numbers one to ten: ọ̀kan, èjì, ẹ̀ta, ẹ̀rin, àrún, ẹ̀fà, èje, ẹ̀jọ, ẹ̀sán, ẹ̀wá. Then teach the forms used with nouns: kan, méjì, mẹ́ta, mẹ́rin, márùn-ún, mẹ́fà, méje, mẹ́jọ, mẹ́sàn-án, mẹ́wàá, with ọmọ kan, ọmọ méjì, ìwé mẹ́ta, and so on.
2. Teach the days: Ọjọ́ Ajé, Ọjọ́ Ìṣẹ́gun, Ọjọ́rú, Ọjọ́bọ̀, Ọjọ́ Ẹtì, Ọjọ́ Àbámẹ́ta, Ọjọ́ Àìkú. Pupils chant them in order starting from Monday.
3. Teach the months with the cards: Ṣẹ̀rẹ̀, Èrèlé, Ẹrẹ̀nà, Igbe, Èbibi, Òkúdù, Agẹmọ, Ògún, Owewe, Ọ̀wàrà, Bélú, Ọ̀pẹ̀. Check against a calendar so pupils see which month is which.
4. Teach the time: Aago mélòó ni? (What time is it?) Aago méjì ni. Add àárọ̀, ọ̀sán, ìrọ̀lẹ́ and alẹ́ to tell the part of the day: aago mẹ́jọ àárọ̀.
5. Use the clock: move the hands and ask the question. Pupils reply in full.
6. Pupils write a three-line timetable in Yoruba.

## Class activity

Group relay: the teacher calls a number, a day or a time. One pupil from each group writes the answer on the board. The first correct written answer with all marks scores a point.

## Evaluation

1. Say the days of the week in order.
2. Write "seven books" in Yoruba.
3. What do you say to ask the time?

## Assignment

Worksheet on the app, due Friday.

reading.content:
# Nọ́ńbà, ọjọ́ àti àkókò ní èdè Yorùbá

## Nọ́ńbà kan sí mẹ́wàá

Nígbà tí a bá ń ka nọ́ńbà lásán, a máa ń sọ pé:

| Nọ́ńbà | Yorùbá | Pẹ̀lú orúkọ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | ọ̀kan | ọmọ kan |
| 2 | èjì | ọmọ méjì |
| 3 | ẹ̀ta | ọmọ mẹ́ta |
| 4 | ẹ̀rin | ọmọ mẹ́rin |
| 5 | àrún | ọmọ márùn-ún |
| 6 | ẹ̀fà | ọmọ mẹ́fà |
| 7 | èje | ọmọ méje |
| 8 | ẹ̀jọ | ọmọ mẹ́jọ |
| 9 | ẹ̀sán | ọmọ mẹ́sàn-án |
| 10 | ẹ̀wá | ọmọ mẹ́wàá |

Àpẹẹrẹ: Mo ní ìwé mẹ́ta. Ọmọ márùn-ún wà nínú kíláàsì.

## Ọjọ́ méje nínú ọ̀sẹ̀

1. Ọjọ́ Ajé (Monday)
2. Ọjọ́ Ìṣẹ́gun (Tuesday)
3. Ọjọ́rú (Wednesday)
4. Ọjọ́bọ̀ (Thursday)
5. Ọjọ́ Ẹtì (Friday)
6. Ọjọ́ Àbámẹ́ta (Saturday)
7. Ọjọ́ Àìkú (Sunday)

Àwọn ọmọ ilé ìwé máa ń lọ sí ilé ìwé láti Ọjọ́ Ajé dé Ọjọ́ Ẹtì.

## Oṣù méjìlá nínú ọdún

Ṣẹ̀rẹ̀, Èrèlé, Ẹrẹ̀nà, Igbe, Èbibi, Òkúdù, Agẹmọ, Ògún, Owewe, Ọ̀wàrà, Bélú, Ọ̀pẹ̀.

Ṣẹ̀rẹ̀ ni oṣù kìíní, Ọ̀pẹ̀ sì ni oṣù kejìlá.

## Àkókò ọjọ́

- àárọ̀: morning
- ọ̀sán: afternoon
- ìrọ̀lẹ́: evening
- alẹ́ / òru: night

## Bí a ṣe ń sọ àkókò

Ìbéèrè: Aago mélòó ni?
Ìdáhùn: Aago méjì ni. (It is two o'clock.)

Fi àkókò ọjọ́ kún un: aago mẹ́jọ àárọ̀ (8 in the morning), aago méjì ọ̀sán (2 in the afternoon), aago mẹ́fà ìrọ̀lẹ́ (6 in the evening).

Àpẹẹrẹ: Ilé ìwé máa ń bẹ̀rẹ̀ ní aago mẹ́jọ àárọ̀.

## Àkọsílẹ̀ ètò ọjọ́

Ọjọ́ Ajé, aago mẹ́jọ àárọ̀: mo lọ sí ilé ìwé.
Ọjọ́ Ẹtì, aago méjì ọ̀sán: mo ń ṣeré bọ́ọ̀lù.

## Àṣìṣe tí ó wọ́pọ̀

- Kíkọ nọ́ńbà láìsí àmì ohùn: mẹ́ta, kì í ṣe "meta".
- Kíkọ "Ojo Aje" dípò "Ọjọ́ Ajé".
- Lílo "aago" láìsọ nọ́ńbà.

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Nọ́ńbà tí a fi ń ka nǹkan yàtọ̀ sí èyí tí a fi ń ka lásán. Kọ gbogbo àmì ohùn.
